title: Thoughts on Raijin.trade?
author: philosohpyofunity
selftext: I've been backtesting, paper trading, and exploring Raijin.  Wanted to hear from anyone else about their experience with them or if you've used real capital on their platform.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: never used Raijin, so nothing on them specifically. before real money on any of these I'd check two things: whether options fill at the mid or at the bid and ask, and whether a backtest can only see data that existed at that bar. those two are what I built Quantradin around, it's free and paper only: quantradin.com. are you testing stocks or options on it?

replies.author: philosohpyofunity
replies.body:
Long only socks, no options.  They also do crypto and prediction markets, but I prefer and know stocks best.

It can only read one 1-minute completed candle bar at a time and currently their backtest can only go back to Jan of this year.  So no tick reading and nothing under 1min (so could technically check intrabar for a 15min candle).  Though if the test involves checking every minute Ive found it struggles to complete 3 months of data before failing due to what I assume to be too many "fires".

It does best with higher timeframes it seems.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Jan to now worries me more than the 1 min cap. That's one stretch of tape, mostly up, so a long-only rule looks better than it is. I hit the same wall and built Quantradin for it (stocks on daily or minute bars, and it grades the rule instead of just drawing the curve), free and runs on paper.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Useful detail, thanks. Those limits matter for how much to trust a result: with only data back to January, a stretch of about nine months is one market regime, so I'd treat any backtest there as a rough sketch and not a test. Since it reads one closed 1-minute bar at a time, stops and targets can only be checked at bar close, so any strategy that depends on exact intrabar fills will look better in the backtest than live. The failures after too many fires may also mean you only see partial runs, so I'd check that the trade count matches what you expect before trusting any equity curve. Higher timeframes make sense for it, since the fill assumptions matter less there.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I haven't used Raijin, so I can't speak to the platform, but for any tool you've been paper trading on, the step before real capital is checking how the paper results were made. Compare a handful of paper fills with the actual quotes at the time, find out how the backtest handles fees and slippage, and ask who holds your funds and whether the platform can touch withdrawals. If you do go live, start with a small amount and run the same rules next to the paper account for a few weeks, so you can see how far real fills drift from the paper ones. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to see how strategy results get compared against a benchmark.
